evidence:
Defining behaviour is graded. The product is a custom code editor plus isolated Run plus a shared saved library with revisions (instruction.md; overview.md:3-5). tests/scored/functional/judge.toml grades editing through real keys and mouse (cw_custom_typing_and_line_join line 24 onward, multi-caret, find/replace, format), running (cw_basic_run_output, line 213: 'Press Run: the preview must show the correct sum and the app console must contain it', then a changed integer must give the new sum, so a canned preview fails), and saving (lines 339-398). The render gate is only load-and-type, so the working-Run proof sits in a scored criterion rather than a gate; that still satisfies 'at least one criterion proves the defining behaviour'.

Durability is proven at three levels, each with a public requirement (behaviour.md:9 'A fresh page must read the saved record from the running app, and saved work and history must survive a complete server restart'; integration.md:7 and :9). (1) Reload and server-backed: tests/gates/constraints/judge.toml:27-32 cw_shared_saved_record, an all_pass gate: 'clear this origin's browser storage as described in the application notes and reload the page, so nothing held only in the browser survives. Find that snippet in the library, open it and confirm the exact title, filename and source. Reload once more'. app_context.md:25 defines the clearing as localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB, Cache Storage, the origin private file system, service worker registrations and cookies. This is the right answer to the workbook's 'server-backed is not same-origin' caveat: the proof does not rest on the request going to localhost, it rests on the record surviving removal of every origin store. (2) Process restart: functional judge.toml:339-345 cw_save_reload_restart repeats the storage clear, then 'call the verifier-provided restart_app tool once. After it reports a completed restart, a fresh page must show the same single record with the same revision, title, filename, source and history. Do not infer a restart from a reload or a health response', and fails if the tool errors. The tool is wired (functional judge.toml:14-18), functional/prompt.md:29-31 restricts it to that criterion, and tests/test.sh and tests/tools/restart_mcp.py are byte-identical to the frozen template; the helper kills the process group and relaunches with the same DB_PATH (test.sh:154-167). (3) Cross-tab server truth: cw_stale_save_refused (line 348) requires 'A fresh read of the record in a third page or after a reload', and cw_history_restore_retry (line 366) reads history 'in a freshly loaded page'. No sign-in exists, so re-authentication does not apply.

Weak apps tried: a localStorage or IndexedDB library fails the constraints gate after the storage clear, so reward is 0; a server keeping snippets in a Map passes the gate but fails cw_save_reload_restart after the real restart; a static shell fails the render gate; an app whose Run is dead fails cw_basic_run_output and every Run-dependent criterion. Conforming alternative tried: an app with different routes, a file layout of its own and a save response that does not echo fields still passes, because the gate says 'the response need not echo the saved fields', app_context.md:23 says records are identified by the server and the library may be non-empty, and no route is assumed.

Run evidence. Scripted golden on these exact bytes (hashes verified): persist-before.json has cw_shared_saved_record true and cw_save_reload_restart(before) true; restart.log shows a real process replacement (pid_before 37, pid_after 66); persist-after.json has cw_save_reload_restart true; restart.json shows record id 3 at revision 2 with history [2,1] carried across. Hosted configured judge on an EARLIER candidate: both criteria scored 1.0, their description text in reward-details.json is word for word the current text, and the judge reported 'restart complete: the server was relaunched on the same database and answers HTTP' followed by the same single record #3. Limits: no configured judge run exists for these bytes; the scripted run restarted with pkill rather than the test.sh helper and cleared only localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB and cookies (persist.cjs:55, :68), a subset of what app_context.md:25 lists. These do not change the verdict because the criterion text and harness for this row are unchanged from what the hosted run exercised.

Residual observations, not defects (P3, no observed impact): (a) integration.md:7 says the library 'must be shared between independent browser contexts', but no criterion requires a genuinely separate browser context; app_context.md:25 accepts 'any two pages' and substitutes storage clearing. That is an adequate proxy for origin storage. (b) The gate's readback is a reload in the same tab, so stores the clearing script cannot reach (window.name, the URL, an HttpOnly cookie) would survive it; the restart criterion's 'fresh page' covers window.name, and none of these is a plausible builder design for a multi-record library that must also update live across tabs.
